construct: In a 46,XY individual with functioning testes, Sertoli-cell anti-Müllerian hormone causes regression of Müllerian structures, but absent androgen receptor signaling prevents masculinization of external genitalia and causes sparse pubic/axillary hair. Aromatization of testicular androgens permits normal breast development at puberty.

adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: Primary amenorrhea with normal breasts, sparse pubic hair, absent uterus, male-range testosterone, and a 46,XY karyotype identifies complete androgen insensitivity syndrome.
adversarial_second_pass.strongest_distractor_attack: Mayer-Rokitansky-Küster-Hauser syndrome also causes an absent uterus and primary amenorrhea, but patients are 46,XX with normal ovarian androgen levels and normal pubic hair.
adversarial_second_pass.expert_reviewer_reversal: The 46,XY karyotype, male-range testosterone, and sparse androgen-dependent hair make complete androgen insensitivity uniquely correct.
